data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's position is sustainable only if we accept a 'propensity' interpretation of probability, where corroboration reflects the objective tendency of a theory to withstand tests, thereby allowing a non-inductive basis for preference.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If propensities are themselves unobservable and metaphysically dubious.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If measuring propensity still requires assuming the future resembles the past.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's own writings on propensity are inconsistent with his earlier rejection of probability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Introduce Popper's propensity theory as the missing link. The mechanism posits that theories have an objective 'propensity' to survive tests based on their fit with reality. Corroboration is the measure of this propensity. Preferring the better-corroborated theory is thus preferring the one with the higher objective propensity to be true (or close to it), which is a factual claim about the world, not an inductive inference from past to future.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
